function.name: search_google
function.description: Performs a search query on Google and returns a list of URLs that match the search criteria. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term to query on Google.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. The number must be a positive integer.

language.description: The language for the search results.

filter.description: A flag to filter explicit content in search results.

date_range.description: The date range for the search results in the format 'MM/DD/YYYY-MM/DD/YYYY'. If not specified, searches across all dates.

message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most prominent vaccine manufacturers around the world (and a few notable regional players).  If you’d like deeper details—such as product pipelines, recent approvals, or financials—just let me know!

| # | Company | Headquarters | Notable COVID‑19 Vaccines (or other key products) | Other Highlights |
|---|---------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------|
| 1 | **Pfizer‑BioNTech** | New York, USA / Mainz, Germany | BNT162b2 (Comirnaty) – mRNA | First mRNA vaccine to receive WHO emergency use listing; strong oncology pipeline |
| 2 | **Moderna** | Cambridge, USA | mRNA‑1273 (Spikevax) – mRNA | Rapid mRNA platform; expanding to influenza and RSV |
| 3 | **Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)** | New Brunswick, USA | Ad26.COV2.S (Janssen) – viral vector | Single‑dose regimen; also produces vaccines for meningitis, HPV |
| 4 | **AstraZeneca** | Cambridge, UK | AZD1222 (Vaxzevria) – adenovirus vector | Global distribution; also developing malaria and TB vaccines |
| 5 | **Novavax** | Gaithersburg, USA | NVX-CoV2373 (Nuvaxovid) – protein subunit | Strong safety profile; also working on influenza and RSV |
| 6 | **Sinovac Biotech** | Beijing, China | CoronaVac – inactivated virus | Widely used in Asia, Latin America, and Africa |
| 7 | **Sinopharm (Hepatitis B, inactivated)** | Beijing, China | BBIBP‑CorV – inactivated virus | Large domestic market; also produces hepatitis B and influenza |
| 8 | **Bharat Biotech** | Hyderabad, India | Covaxin – inactivated virus | First Indian‑made COVID vaccine; also produces vaccines for typhoid, hepatitis B |
| 9 | **CureVac** | Tübingen, Germany | CVnCoV (mRNA) – under development | Focus on mRNA platform; also working on influenza |
|10 | **GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)** | Brentford, UK | Various vaccines (e.g., HPV, influenza, meningitis) | One of the largest global vaccine producers; strong R&D in infectious diseases |
|11 | **Sanofi Pasteur** | Paris, France | Various vaccines (e.g., influenza, meningitis, HPV) | Global distribution network; strong focus on emerging diseases |
|12 | **Merck & Co. (MSD)** | Kenilworth, USA | Various vaccines (e.g., HPV, influenza, rabies) | Strong oncology and diabetes portfolio; active in vaccine R&D |
|13 | **GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)** | Brentford, UK | Various vaccines (e.g., HPV, influenza, meningitis) | One of the largest global vaccine producers; strong R&D in infectious diseases |
|14 | **Biontech** | Mainz, Germany | mRNA‑1273 (Spikevax) – mRNA | Joint venture with Pfizer; strong focus on mRNA therapeutics |
|15 | **Serum Institute of India** | Pune, India | Various vaccines (e.g., polio, measles, influenza) | Largest vaccine manufacturer by volume; supplies WHO and UNICEF |

### Quick Tips for Further Exploration
- **Regulatory Status**: Check WHO’s Emergency Use Listing (EUL) or FDA/EMA approvals for the latest status.
- **Supply Chains**: Look into each company’s manufacturing sites—especially for mRNA vaccines, which require ultra‑cold storage.
- **Pipeline**: Many of these companies are diversifying beyond COVID‑19 into influenza, RSV, malaria, and other infectious diseases.

Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into any particular company, their financials, or upcoming vaccine candidates!
